name: Bluegill Marsh
summary: Bluegill Marsh lies in western Wetlands, where the Bluegill tribe claims the shallows. Gobbler guards their huts and waterways, and travelers risk being surrounded.

sections.title: A Swarming Hazard
sections.body: Bluegill murlocs crowd the muddy flats and reeds of western Wetlands. Their tribe has built crude camps in the stagnant water and claims the marsh. They live and hunt in close-knit packs. Travelers and scouts from Menethil Harbor risk ambush from every side when they wade into Bluegill territory, where chieftain Gobbler prowls the shallows.

faq.answer: Bluegill Marsh is a boggy stretch of western Wetlands and the main home and nesting ground of the aggressive Bluegill murlocs.
Gobbler, a powerful and vicious murloc, rules the Bluegill tribe. He watches over its clustered camps and strikes down land-walkers who enter the waters.

faq.q: Why is it dangerous to travel here alone?
aliases: why are there so many murlocs
faq.answer: Bluegill murlocs gather in bands of two or three around their huts and shorelines. Their numbers and the deep, slowing mud can overwhelm a lone traveler.

faq.q: Why do travelers venture into Bluegill Marsh?
faq.answer: Scouts and adventurers from nearby settlements such as Menethil Harbor enter Bluegill Marsh to thin the aggressive murloc population and recover stolen goods from their camps.

angles.text: Near Menethil Harbor, aggressive Bluegill murlocs threaten travelers and supply lines crossing western Wetlands.
